newsitem.title: USA: Cyrix jumps on better-than-expected profits.
newsitem.headline: Cyrix jumps on better-than-expected profits.

text.p: Cyrix Corp. stock jumped about 23 percent Thursday after the computer chip maker reported first-quarter profits three times better than Wall Street had expected.
Shares of Cyrix, which makes microprocessors to run personal computers, soared by $4 to $21.75 on the Nasdaq market, where it was one of the most actively traded issues.
After the market closed Thursday, Cyrix said its first-quarter net income more than tripled to $6.6 million, or 33 cents a share, from $2 million, or 10 cents a share, in the same quarter a year ago.
Wall Street analysts had expected Cyrix to earn 9 cents a share, according to a survey of analysts by Zacks Investment Research.
The company said its first-quarter revenues rose 47 percent to $75.6 million from $51.6 million.
Cyrix, which is based in Richardson, Texas, also said Thursday that it expected brisk business for two of its main products -- its new MediaGX and older 6x86 chips -- for the rest of the year.

The company had much better than expected gross margins -- a measure of how much profit is made on each dollar of product sold -- which showed it had improved its manufacturing effeciency, analysts said.

Cyrix makes microprocessors that mimic the way Intel Corp.'s Pentium chips work. Its MediaGX chip, which was introduced this year, works about as fast as Intel's mid-range Pentiums but is much less expensive.
